item.title: Conspiracy to destabilise country has begun: Tarique

item.title: DSCC truck hits motorcycle, kills 2 univ students
item.description: Two university students were killed early Friday after a Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) garbage truck rammed their motorcycle in the Konapara area of Demra.They were taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) around 5:00am, where on-duty doctors pronounced them dead, said Inspector Md Faruk, in charge of the DMCH police camp.The victims were identified as Iram Redwan, 25, a student of American International University-Bangladesh (AIUB), and Apu Ahmed, 25, a student of United Internation

item.title: Tentulia shivers in cold
item.description: Tentulia, the northernmost upazila of Panchagarh district, experienced a slight rise in temperature on Friday, reaching 9.3°C after dipping to the season's lowest of 8.9°C. item.title: Fire breaks out at high-rise building in Keraniganj
item.description: A fire broke out at the 12-storey Jamela Tower in the Babubazar area of Keraniganj in the capital on Saturday.Fourteen units of the Fire Service and Civil Defence are working to bring the blaze under control.According to Anwarul Islam Dolon, an official of the Fire Service headquarters’ media cell, the fire was reported at 5:37 AM. item.title: Iran seizes oil tanker in Gulf of Oman

item.title: Fire at Laxmipur election office: documents damaged
item.description: A fire broke out at Laxmipur District Election Office early Saturday after miscreants allegedly poured petrol and set the premises ablaze, damaging several important documents stored on the ground floor.According to election office sources, the incident occurred around 3:30 AM when attackers broke a window on the ground floor, poured petrol inside the office and ignited the fire. item.title: Mirza Fakhrul visits Evercare Hospital, inquires about Khaleda Zia, Hadi

item.title: 3.31 lakh expatriates register to vote in 13th JS polls
item.description: A total of 3,30,946 Bangladeshi expatriates have registered through the Postal Vote BD app to vote in the 13th Jatiya Sangsad (JS) Election and the national referendum, the Election Commission (EC) said. Of them, 3, 06,908 are male and 24,038 are female.Country-wise, the highest number of registrations came from Saudi Arabia (91,803), followed by Qatar (29,000), the UAE (21,747), the USA (21,165), Malaysia (20,886), Singapore (16,664), Oman (14,935), the UK (14,337), and Italy (10,576).
